# New-ZbxHttpTestStep

## SYNOPSIS

Builds a web scenario step for the -Step of New-ZbxHttpTest and Set-ZbxHttpTest.

## SYNTAX

```
New-ZbxHttpTestStep [-Name] <string> [-Url] <string> [-StepNumber <int>] [-QueryField <ZabbixHttpTestStepQueryFieldRequest[]>] [-Posts <JsonElement>] [-Variable <ZabbixHttpTestStepVariableRequest[]>] [-Header <ZabbixHttpTestStepHeaderRequest[]>] [-FollowRedirects <bool>] [-RetrieveMode <ZabbixHttpTestRetrieveMode>] [-Timeout <string>] [-Required <string>] [-StatusCodes <string>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A step is one request of a web scenario: its URL, what it posts, and the status codes and text it expects back. The New-ZbxHttpTestStep cmdlet writes it as a hashtable keyed by the API's field names, which the -Step of New-ZbxHttpTest and Set-ZbxHttpTest take as it is, alone or in an array. -Name and -Url are positional. Nothing is sent to the server, so the command needs no connection.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Build a step that expects a status code

```powershell
New-ZbxHttpTestStep 'Home page' 'https://shop.example.com/' -StatusCodes '200'
```

-Name and -Url are positional; -StatusCodes is a list or ranges such as 200,301-302.

### Example 2: Build a step that posts a form and checks the answer

```powershell
New-ZbxHttpTestStep 'Log in' 'https://shop.example.com/login' -Posts @{ name = 'user'; value = 'monitor' }, @{ name = 'password'; value = '{$SHOP.PASSWORD}' } -Required 'Welcome' -Timeout '15s'
```

-Posts are the form fields, -Required is text (or a regular expression) the answer must contain, and {$SHOP.PASSWORD} is a user macro the server resolves when it runs the step.
